messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — we're starting a canary of the new console render pipeline at 17:00 PT. It switches panel fanout to an async, queued worker model with per-tenant backpressure. Short version: should cut p99 render latency for small dashboards, but introduces a bounded queue and a fallback path for heavy queries. Please review ASAP, need SRE + Query + Auth signoff.

andrew: @maria can you call out the fallback behaviour? if a tenant saturates the queue do we block, drop, or fallback to sync fanout?

maria: good q. plan is: queue_limit: 200 per-tenant, per-worker. when queue >= threshold we route to the legacy sync fanout for that request (best-effort) and emit a counter `console.render.fallback`. no silent drops. snippet of config we're testing:```yaml
render_pipeline:
  workers: 16
  per_tenant_queue_limit: 200
  fallback: sync_fanout
  backpressure_window_ms: 1000
```

sara: how does this interact with RBAC? we currently short-circuit some authz checks inline for fast-paths — moving to async could change timing/visibility. could we end up rendering data before permission checks finish? :worried:

maria: authz remains synchronous on the incoming request thread — we prefetch permission set and attach a signed header to the queued job. worker will validate header + token before materializing panels. we'll add an assertion in canary to ensure no render job proceeds without valid auth header.

kevin: ops question — what SLO impact do we expect during cutover? if we route to sync_fanout more often, p95 might spike. do we have a runbook to roll back if p95 > 200ms for more than 5m?

maria: agreed. rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours with automated rollback if p95 or error-rate breach. runbook excerpt: `if p95_render_latency > 200ms for 5m OR render_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m => revert to previous configuration`.

andrew: can you share the prometheus queries we'll use for the canary dashboard? I want to wire alerts.

kevin: putting this here:```promql
rate(console_render_requests_total[1m]) by (tenant)
increase(console_render_fallback_total[5m])
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(console_render_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

sara: also add an authz-failure metric. if a worker rejects a job due to missing/invalid header we need a clear counter `console.render.auth_rejects` and alert on >0.1% of render attempts.

maria: will add. also adding instrumentation to correlate fallback events with tenant_id so we can spot noisy tenants quickly.

devops-bot: deploy:console-render-pipeline canary started by @maria — canary id c-20231011-7. 3 workers in this canary.

kevin: thanks. I'll stand by for alerts. if we see fallbacks spiking for a tenant > 5m we should proactively throttle that tenant and open a ticket. :eyes: 

andrew: lgtm from query-team perspective, but we should do a small loadtest simulating a heavy multi-panel dashboard to validate KV cache warmup under async path. I can run that at 15:30 PT.

maria: awesome — thanks everyone. I'll post postmortem notes in #postmortems and update the rollout doc with the final config. :rocket:
